check_name: Ensure access is controlled through SSO and not AWS IAM defined users
article_title: Human resources security, access control policies and asset management
risk: Long-lived IAM users bypass centralized identity management and SSO, making it difficult to enforce MFA, audit access centrally, and revoke credentials quickly during an incident. NIS2 Art. 21(2)(i) requires effective access control policies.
remediation:
Delete standing IAM users and federate access through AWS IAM Identity Center (SSO):
  # Remove:
  # resource "aws_iam_user" "admin" { ... }
  # Use Identity Center permission sets + account assignments instead
  # (managed via aws_ssoadmin_* resources or the Identity Center console).

check_name: Ensure AWS IAM policy does not allow full IAM privileges
article_title: Confidentiality, integrity, availability and resilience of processing systems
risk: A policy granting full iam:* lets its holder create users, roles, and policies — including new admin access — so privilege escalation is one API call away. This weakens the access control NIS2 Art. 21(2)(i) requires and endangers all personal data under GDPR Art. 32(1)(b).
remediation:
Never grant iam:* ; scope the few IAM actions genuinely needed:
  # Before:
  "Action": "iam:*"
  # After:
  "Action": ["iam:PassRole"]
  "Resource": aws_iam_role.app.arn

check_name: Ensure IAM policies does not allow privilege escalation
article_title: Confidentiality, integrity, availability and resilience of processing systems
risk: Actions such as iam:PassRole, iam:AttachUserPolicy, or iam:PutUserPolicy allow a low-privileged principal to grant itself higher privileges, collapsing access control (NIS2 Art. 21(2)(i)) and putting the confidentiality of all data at risk.
remediation:
Remove privilege-management actions from workload policies, or constrain them
with a permissions boundary and explicit resource ARNs:
  "Action": ["iam:PassRole"]
  "Resource": "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/app-task-role"
  "Condition": { "StringEquals": { "iam:PassedToService": "ecs-tasks.amazonaws.com" } }

check_name: Ensure IAM policies does not allow credentials exposure
article_title: Confidentiality, integrity, availability and resilience of processing systems
risk: Policies that permit credential-generation actions (sts:GetFederationToken, iam:CreateAccessKey, ec2:GetPasswordData, etc.) let an attacker mint new credentials and pivot, undermining the confidentiality controls GDPR Art. 32(1)(b) requires and the access control NIS2 Art. 21(2)(i) mandates.
remediation:
Remove credential-exposing actions and scope to least privilege:
  # Before:
  "Action": ["sts:*", "iam:CreateAccessKey"]
  # After:
  "Action": ["s3:GetObject", "s3:PutObject"]
  "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::my-app-data/*"

check_name: Ensure IAM policies does not allow data exfiltration
article_title: Confidentiality, integrity, availability and resilience of processing systems
risk: Broad read actions on all resources (s3:GetObject, secretsmanager:GetSecretValue, rds:DownloadDBLogFilePortion on "*") enable bulk exfiltration of data — if that data is personal, an exfiltration path through them could lead to a personal data breach.   "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::approved-bucket/*"

check_name: Ensure IAM policies that allow full "*-*" administrative privileges are not created
article_title: Confidentiality, integrity, availability and resilience of processing systems
risk: A policy granting Action "*" on Resource "*" is unrestricted administrative access. It can weaken least privilege and access segregation, and gives any holder the ability to read, alter, or destroy all data - which may weaken both NIS2 Art. 21(2)(i) and the confidentiality/integrity goals of GDPR Art. 32(1)(b).
remediation:
Replace the wildcard grant with explicit, scoped statements:
  # Before:
  "Action": "*"
  "Resource": "*"
  # After:
  "Action": ["s3:GetObject", "s3:PutObject"]
  "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::my-app-data/*"

check_name: Ensure VPC flow logging is enabled in all VPCs
article_title: Incident handling
risk: Without VPC flow logs there is no network-level record of accepted/rejected connections, so lateral movement and exfiltration attempts cannot be detected or reconstructed. NIS2 Art. 21(2)(b) requires detection and analysis of incidents.
remediation:
Enable flow logs for the VPC:
  resource "aws_flow_log" "this" {
    vpc_id          = aws_vpc.main.id
    traffic_type    = "ALL"
    log_destination = aws_cloudwatch_log_group.vpc_flow.arn
    iam_role_arn    = aws_iam_role.vpc_flow.arn
  }

check_name: Ensure the default security group of every VPC restricts all traffic
article_title: Human resources security, access control policies and asset management
risk: An unmanaged default security group can implicitly allow traffic between any resources that fall back to it, bypassing intended segmentation. NIS2 Art. 21(2)(i) expects deliberate, least-privilege network access control.

check_name: Ensure that Security Groups are attached to another resource
article_title: Human resources security, access control policies and asset management
risk: Orphaned security groups accumulate stale rules that later get attached "because they were there", importing unintended access into live environments — an unmanaged asset under the access control and asset management of NIS2 Art. 21(2)(i).

check_name: Ensure every security group and rule has a description
article_title: Human resources security, access control policies and asset management
risk: Undocumented rules cannot be reviewed: nobody can tell which rule is a deliberate control and which is leftover access. Descriptions are what make rule review — and therefore accountable access control under NIS2 Art. 21(2)(i) — possible.

check_name: Ensure no security groups allow ingress from 0.0.0.0:0 to port 22
article_title: Confidentiality, integrity, availability and resilience of processing systems
risk: SSH (port 22) open to 0.0.0.0/0 exposes administrative shell access to the entire internet, inviting brute-force and exploitation of any host that may process personal data. This may weaken the network access-control measures relevant to NIS2 Art. 21(2)(i) and the confidentiality safeguards expected by GDPR Art. 32(1)(b).
remediation:
Restrict SSH to a bastion or corporate CIDR, never the internet. Remove the
wildcard in both address families when both attributes are present:
  resource "aws_security_group" "admin" {
    ingress {
      from_port        = 22
      to_port          = 22
      protocol         = "tcp"
      # Before: cidr_blocks = ["0.0.0.0/0"]

article_title: Business continuity, backup management and disaster recovery

check_name: Ensure that enhanced monitoring is enabled for Amazon RDS instances
article_title: Incident handling

check_name: Ensure that respective logs of Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS) are enabled

check_name: Ensure that S3 bucket has cross-region replication enabled
article_title: Ability to restore availability and access to personal data in a timely manner
risk: A bucket replicated only in one region is lost with that region. Cross-region replication is the mechanism that keeps personal data available and restorable after a regional outage, relevant to NIS2 Art. 21(2)(c) and GDPR Art. 32(1)(c).

check_name: Ensure S3 bucket has block public ACLS enabled

check_name: Ensure S3 bucket does not allow an action with any Principal
article_title: Confidentiality, integrity, availability and resilience of processing systems
risk: A bucket policy statement whose Principal is "*" makes the bucket world-accessible for the listed actions — exposing any personal data in it to unauthenticated access and creating a potential control gap relevant to the access-control measures in NIS2 Art. 21(2)(i) and the confidentiality safeguards expected by GDPR Art. 32(1)(b).

    "Action": ["s3:GetObject"],
    "Resource": "arn:aws:s3:::my-app-data/*"
  }
